title: Meta delays new business terms to 20 November after publisher pushback
friendlyTitle: Meta has delayed new business terms to 20 November
summary: Meta is delaying enforcement of new business terms from 30 October to 20 November, spokesperson Daniel Roberts told The Verge. Publishers had warned that the terms could let Meta scrape news sites that use its tools, including for AI training. Meta had already removed the word 'training' from the terms. Legal experts told The Verge that edit was not enough to rule training out. Roberts said the delay is time to explain how Meta's crawlers work, and that content owners can still use robots.txt to signal what they do not want crawled.
friendlySummary: Meta is delaying its new business terms from 30 October to 20 November. Spokesperson Daniel Roberts told The Verge the extra time is to explain what is changing. Publishers had warned that the terms could let Meta scrape news sites that use its tools, including for AI training. Meta had already removed the word 'training.' Legal experts told The Verge that edit was not enough to rule training out. Roberts said content owners can still use a robots.txt file to say what they do not want crawled.
whyItMatters: If your site uses Meta's business tools, the practical date is now 20 November, not the end of this month. A robots.txt file is still the control Meta is pointing to. It is a signal, not a lock, and it only helps if you have set it before a crawler arrives. The dispute is whether the contract, even without the word 'training,' still lets Meta use what it collects to build models.
